runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In HTTPBearer.authenticate within buggy_impl.py, when an authorization header contains a scheme other than 'bearer', AuthenticationError is raised unconditionally regardless of whether self.auto_error is True or False.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/fastapi_optional_bearer/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if scheme.casefold() != "bearer":
            raise AuthenticationError("Invalid authentication credentials")' with 'if scheme.casefold() != "bearer":
            if self.auto_error:
                raise AuthenticationError("Invalid authentication credentials")
            return None'. When auto_error is False, non-Bearer schemes should not raise an AuthenticationError but instead return None, matching the optional dependency contract.
Regression check: verify() creates an HTTPBearer instance with auto_error=False and asserts authenticate(None) is None, authenticate('Basic abc123') is None, and authenticate('Bearer token-7') returns ('Bearer', 'token-7'). (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/fastapi_optional_bearer/check.py).

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `update_headers`, unset headers have a value of `None`. Calling `value.decode("utf8")` unconditionally raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode'` when encountering an unset header sentinel.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        value = value.decode("utf8")' with 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        value = value.decode("utf8")'. Check whether the header value is None before calling `.decode('utf8')` and skip adding unset headers to the updated headers dictionary.
Regression check: The test `verify` in `check.py` invokes `update_headers` with `{"Authorization": None, "X-Request-ID": b"request-7"}` and asserts that the resulting dictionary is `{"X-Request-ID": "request-7"}`. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/check.py).

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `rendered_headers`, `headers` is constructed as a standard Python `dict(original.items())`. The membership check `if "Host" not in headers:` performs a case-sensitive lookup on the plain dictionary rather than querying `original` (which implements case-insensitive membership via `__contains__`). Consequently, when `original` contains lowercase `'host'`, `'Host'` is reported missing and re-added, duplicating the header.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if "Host" not in headers:' with 'if "Host" not in original:'. Checking membership against the plain dictionary `headers` uses case-sensitive lookup, ignoring the case-insensitive lookup implemented on `original`. Checking `if "Host" not in original:` uses `CaseInsensitiveHeaders.__contains__`, preventing duplicate host entries when a case-variant header like 'host' already exists.
Regression check: The test `verify` in check.py passes a `CaseInsensitiveHeaders` instance initialized with `[("host", "custom.example")]` to `rendered_headers` and asserts that only `["custom.example"]` is present for case-folded 'host' keys. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/check.py).

params.diagnosis: In `rendered_headers`, `headers` is constructed as a standard Python `dict(original.items())`. The membership check `if "Host" not in headers:` performs a case-sensitive lookup on the plain dictionary rather than querying `original` (which implements case-insensitive membership via `__contains__`). Consequently, when `original` contains lowercase `'host'`, `'Host'` is reported missing and re-added, duplicating the header.

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `APIRouter.include_router`, iteration over `child.routes` only handles routes of type `APIRoute` and ignores instances of `WebSocketRoute`, causing websocket routes from child routers to be dropped during router inclusion.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/fastapi_websocket_router/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if isinstance(route, APIRoute):
                self.routes.append(APIRoute(prefix + route.path, route.name))' with 'if isinstance(route, APIRoute):
                self.routes.append(APIRoute(prefix + route.path, route.name))
            elif isinstance(route, WebSocketRoute):
                self.routes.append(WebSocketRoute(prefix + route.path, route.name))'. In `APIRouter.include_router`, check whether each child route is an instance of `WebSocketRoute` in addition to `APIRoute`, appending a corresponding `WebSocketRoute` with the prefix prepended to the path and preserving its name.
Regression check: `check.verify` includes a child router containing both an APIRoute and a WebSocketRoute under prefix '/v1' into a parent router, and asserts that parent.routes contains prefixed versions of both route types with matching names. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/fastapi_websocket_router/check.py).

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `update_headers`, `value.decode("utf8")` is called unconditionally on each value in `request_headers`. When a session header is explicitly unset, its value is `None`, resulting in an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode'`.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        value = value.decode("utf8")' with 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        value = value.decode("utf8")'. Check whether `value` is `None` before calling `.decode("utf8")` and skip unset headers so that `None` is not decoded and unset headers are omitted from the updated headers mapping.
Regression check: Calls `verify` in check.py, which passes `{"Authorization": None, "X-Request-ID": b"request-7"}` to `update_headers` and asserts that the resulting dictionary is `{"X-Request-ID": "request-7"}`. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/check.py).

output.root_cause: `rendered_headers` converts `CaseInsensitiveHeaders` to a standard case-sensitive Python `dict` via `headers = dict(original.items())` and performs `if "Host" not in headers:`. Because standard dictionary key lookups are case-sensitive, an existing lowercase `"host"` header is not matched by `"Host"`, causing `headers["Host"] = url_host` to be inserted and duplicating the host header.
verification_steps: Construct `original = CaseInsensitiveHeaders([("host", "custom.example")])`.
Call `rendered_headers(original, "url.example")`.
Filter the resulting dictionary items for keys matching `"host"` case-insensitively.
Assert that the extracted host values list equals `["custom.example"]`.

output.corrective_action:
Root cause: In `rendered_headers`, converting `original` to a standard Python `dict` loses the case-insensitive containment behavior of `CaseInsensitiveHeaders`. As a result, `"Host" not in headers` evaluates to `True` when a lowercase `'host'` header is present, causing a duplicate `'Host'` entry to be added.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if "Host" not in headers:' with 'if "Host" not in original:'. Checking membership against the plain `headers` dictionary uses case-sensitive dictionary lookup, ignoring the case-insensitive lookup implemented on `original`. Checking `"Host" not in original` leverages `CaseInsensitiveHeaders.__contains__` to correctly detect existing lowercase or mixed-case Host headers.
Regression check: The test in check.py passes a CaseInsensitiveHeaders instance with a lowercase ('host', 'custom.example') entry to rendered_headers, and asserts that only a single casefolded 'host' header value ('custom.example') is present in the rendered result. runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `rendered_headers`, converting `original` to a standard Python `dict` loses the case-insensitive containment behavior of `CaseInsensitiveHeaders`. As a result, `"Host" not in headers` evaluates to `True` when a lowercase `'host'` header is present, causing a duplicate `'Host'` entry to be added.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if "Host" not in headers:' with 'if "Host" not in original:'. Checking membership against the plain `headers` dictionary uses case-sensitive dictionary lookup, ignoring the case-insensitive lookup implemented on `original`. Checking `"Host" not in original` leverages `CaseInsensitiveHeaders.__contains__` to correctly detect existing lowercase or mixed-case Host headers.
Regression check: The test in check.py passes a CaseInsensitiveHeaders instance with a lowercase ('host', 'custom.example') entry to rendered_headers, and asserts that only a single casefolded 'host' header value ('custom.example') is present in the rendered result. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/check.py).

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: Inside `get_write_function` in `buggy_impl.py`, the nested `write` closure attempts to open `output_path`, which is undefined in scope because the parameter is named `output`. This causes a `NameError: name 'output_path' is not defined` when writing to a path or string target.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/pysnooper_path_output/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'with open(output_path, "a") as output_file:  # noqa: F821' with 'with open(output, "a") as output_file:'. Replace the undefined variable `output_path` with the parameter `output` within `write`, allowing `open()` to correctly open the destination path/string and removing the unused `# noqa: F821` comment.
Regression check: `check.py` defines `verify(implementation)` which creates a `Path` object, obtains a writer via `get_write_function(output)`, invokes it with a trace string, and asserts that the file contains the expected text. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/pysnooper_path_output/check.py).

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In `update_headers`, unset headers are represented with `None` as their value. The function calls `value.decode("utf8")` unconditionally on each header value in `request_headers.items()`, causing an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode'` when an unset header (`None`) is encountered.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        value = value.decode("utf8")' with 'for name, value in request_headers.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        value = value.decode("utf8")'. Check whether `value` is `None` before attempting to decode it as UTF-8. If `value is None`, skip adding it to `headers` (or `continue`), so unset headers with `None` values are ignored and do not trigger an `AttributeError`.
Regression check: Runs `verify(implementation)` with `{"Authorization": None, "X-Request-ID": b"request-7"}` and asserts that the resulting dictionary is `{"X-Request-ID": "request-7"}` without crashing on `None`. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_unset_header/check.py).

output.corrective_action:
Root cause: In rendered_headers, the presence check `if "Host" not in headers:` operates on the standard Python dict `headers` instead of the case-insensitive collection `original`. Consequently, when an existing header is provided with lowercase casing ('host'), the membership test evaluates to True for absence, adding a duplicate 'Host' key from url_host.

Checking `original` leverages CaseInsensitiveHeaders.__contains__, properly detecting existing Host headers regardless of case.

runtime.final_answer:
Root cause: In rendered_headers, the presence check `if "Host" not in headers:` operates on the standard Python dict `headers` instead of the case-insensitive collection `original`. Consequently, when an existing header is provided with lowercase casing ('host'), the membership test evaluates to True for absence, adding a duplicate 'Host' key from url_host.
Implicated source: file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/buggy_impl.py
Correction: replace 'if "Host" not in headers:' with 'if "Host" not in original:'. Checking membership against `headers` performs a case-sensitive dict lookup, which fails to recognize lowercase keys like 'host'. Checking `original` leverages CaseInsensitiveHeaders.__contains__, properly detecting existing Host headers regardless of case.
Regression check: The test verify() creates CaseInsensitiveHeaders with ('host', 'custom.example'), calls rendered_headers with url_host 'url.example', and asserts that only the single custom host value exists. (file:///Users/rajkumar/Documents/workspace/polya-brain/evals/chapter_13k/fixtures/httpie_host_case/check.py).

Correction: replace 'def serialize_response(response: ResponseModel, *, skip_defaults: bool) -> dict[str, str | None]:\n    value = {"name": response.name, "note": response.note}\n    return dict(value)' with 'def serialize_response(response: ResponseModel, *, skip_defaults: bool) -> dict[str, str | None]:\n    return response.dict(skip_defaults=skip_defaults)'. Delegating to `response.dict(skip_defaults=skip_defaults)` preserves model serialization semantics and properly excludes unset or default fields when `skip_defaults=True`.
